text:
If you’re planning a waterfront walk or a round of errands, the clear start won’t last all day. Clouds will fill in, with a high near 71 and a north wind building from 7 to 13 mph, gusting around 23. The forecast is mainly dry for Burlington, though the models are unusually split on the afternoon temperature, from the upper 60s to mid 70s. I’d favor the NWS middle ground, and leave the rain jacket in the car rather than carry it all day. The lake will be choppier than town, with north winds increasing to 15 to 20 knots and waves up to 2 feet, so keep smaller boats close and expect a cool breeze along the shore. The water is 64, and air quality is good.

Tonight turns cloudier, with a 30 percent chance of showers after 2am. Sunday looks cooler and more unsettled, topping out near 66 with a 40 percent shower chance and north winds around 12 mph. On the lake, winds could reach 25 knots before easing. Enjoy the dry window today, and plan to be off the broad water before the wind strengthens.
